High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

sentences.text:
Heard on I.A. No.1741/2026, which is an application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of sole
appellant - Sanjay.

The present appellant has been convicted for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363,
366, 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code & Section 5(j)(ii)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo 1 year RI with fine of Rs.1000/-, 3 years RI with fine of Rs.1000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5000/-
with default stipulation.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Counsel for the appellant argued that as per statement of prosecutrix, she has performed marriage with the appellant.
He further argued that as per statement of prosecutrix she was aged 20 years on the date of incident, however as per scholar register, prosecution has proved her age to be 13 years and 1 month.
He further argued that date of birth of prosecutrix was recorded in the scholar register on the basis of guess.

He relied on the judgment of Division Bench in the case of Teju Bai Vs. State Of Madhya Pradesh Reported in 2025(1)Criminal 76, where the Division Bench held that if the date of birth of the prosecutix is the school registered is recorded on the guess of the person who had made entry of the date of Birth, the same is not sufficient to proof age of the presecutix.

sentences.text: Counsel further submits that appellant was on bail during trial and he did not misuse the liberty.
The appeal 2 CRA-10586-2025 being of the year 2025 will take time for final hearing.
Hence, remaining jail sentence of the present appellant be suspended.
Counsel for the State has opposed the application.

sentences.text: proved by the prosecution, further the appellant was on bail during trial and he did not misuse the liberty coupled with the fact that appeal will take long time for final hearing, we deem it expedient to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Sanjay shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only)
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.08.2026, and thereafter, on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
